label: OpenCV video quality gate
summary: Optional headless frame sampling for measurable focus, contrast, motion, crop geometry, and thumbnail evidence before a separate human picture review.

handoffs.label: Inspect a video candidate
handoffs.intent: Find measurable blur, low contrast, excessive center-crop loss, or weak thumbnail frames before spending time on a complete manual watch.
inputs: One local video candidate and its intended delivery orientation
Optional focus/contrast thresholds and target width/height
outputs: A ranked thumbnail frame candidate with timestamp and measurable properties
steps: Sample a bounded, evenly spaced set of frames without rewriting the source.
Inspect Laplacian variance, edge density, contrast, sampled frame difference, and crop geometry as evidence only.
Use the report to revise the renderer or framing, then run the ordinary EPRS picture review on the new candidate.
verification: Confirm the source path, decoded sample count, dimensions, frame rate, and thresholds are visible in the report.
Treat a pass as technical evidence, not a creative, sync, rights, publication, or thumbnail approval.
Keep low-motion or intentionally soft visuals available when the brief calls for them; do not turn metrics into a fixed house style.

preserve: The original video, exact sampling parameters, thresholds, and report
The distinction between measurable frame quality and player-facing visual intent
avoid: Overwriting or re-encoding the source, treating a sharp frame as a good film, or rejecting intentional softness without reading the brief
Calling OpenCV from the core render path or making the optional dependency mandatory
